identity.title: Position: AI Agents Need Authenticated Delegation

problem.claim: Autonomous-agent delegation raises authorization, accountability, and access-control challenges.

contributions.claim: Argues that authenticated, auditable delegation should be prioritized in AI-agent governance and outlines a roadmap.
Outlines extending OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect with agent-specific credentials and translating natural-language permissions into scoped rules across interaction modalities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach through agent-specific extensions to established authentication infrastructure and transparent natural-language permission translation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their outlined approach can support clear accountability chains while remaining compatible with established authentication and web infrastructure.
The authors report that the work supports agent systems performing only appropriate actions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Rapid autonomous-agent deployment creates delegation-related authorization, accountability, and access-control challenges.
The paper argues that authenticated and auditable authority delegation is critical for mitigating practical risks and realizing agent value.
It examines extending web protocols and natural-language access-control interfaces for secure agent delegation.
The outlined extensions aim to provide scoped permissions, accountability, infrastructure compatibility, and governance guidance.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects natural-language permissions to robust scoping rules and established authentication protocols.

lessons.interpretation: This frames agent governance as both an interface-translation problem and an accountability-infrastructure problem.
lessons.application: Authors addressing agent safety could map high-level user permissions to explicit scopes and identify the accountability chain supported by each scope.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the task does not involve delegated authority, access control, or auditable actions.

unknowns: The abstract reports no experiments, benchmarks, formal proofs, implementation details, or concrete security analysis.
It does not specify the agent credentials, translation procedure, threat model, or how compatibility and appropriate-action claims are evaluated.
